Foundations and proofs

Chow Obstructions and Prescribed Actual Green Pairs

Actual forms over the original valued field

23 November 2026

Abstract

We construct a rational-linear Chow obstruction with values in the actual Bott–Chern quotient, and an actual curved Green pair for every prescribed rational cycle on a smooth integral projective variety over a finite extension of Qp\mathbf Q_pQp​. The proof retains the original valued field, the exact prescribed support complement, and all compact actual tests. Its inputs are actual model Chern forms, a finite trace on the scalar–curvature module, and supported perfect complexes. We give explicit arguments for the actual/Bedford–Taylor comparison, detection by model Hessians, scalar PL descent with a uniform parameter, and the coordinate Gauss product. The further vanishing of the obstruction on homologically trivial Chow classes is a separate problem.

Relation to the Strong Green programme.

Theorem 1.1 proves the Chow-obstruction and prescribed curved-Green-pair construction formerly stated as Hypothesis 2.2 in the Strong Green programme. Its scope is the original finite extension K/QpK/\mathbf Q_pK/Qp​, every smooth integral projective KKK-variety, the exact prescribed support, and the full space of compact actual tests. The argument below supplies the model-Chern construction, the minimal finite trace, the supported-complex formula, the global primitive, and the integral-scope extension. General vanishing on homologically trivial Chow classes remains a separate assertion.

The proof assembles the model-Chern construction, the scalar–curvature finite trace, and the supported-complex construction. Their proofs, together with the detailed analytic interfaces, are given below. The present theorem does not assume that ZZZ is homologically trivial.

Proof. Step 1: actual model characters. Theorem 2.4 constructs separately closed model characters, strictly additive on model vector-bundle exact sequences and functorial for morphisms of projective flat models. Its proof first establishes the numerical detector for polynomials in model first Chern forms, then descends symmetric root polynomials along local sections of a flag bundle. The actual/CLD comparison and the detector are explained in Section 2. This construction uses no finite trace or prescribed-cycle Green pair.

Step 2: global primitives for generic Chow relations. If a model complex is generically acyclic, apply the supported-complex construction with the entire generic fibre as its exact open. The relative line construction is then finite flat everywhere on that fibre, and its scalar–curvature line sum has empty generic divisor. The trace formula gives a global actual form Ψ\PsiΨ whose DDD is the alternating model character. Actual-current injectivity turns the testing identity into an equality of actual forms. This is the argument of Corollary 8.6; it also covers the empty generic support, for which no codimension is assigned to the empty set.

On a common model, the graph of each generic subbundle yields an exact model sequence. Strict Whitney reduces the original relation to differences of model extensions of isomorphic generic bundles. After uniformizer rescaling, these differences are represented by generically acyclic two-term complexes. Adding their primitives proves Proposition 8.7.

2. Model Chern forms: the measure comparison and descent interfaces

Fix a finite extension K/QpK/\mathbf Q_pK/Qp​ with its given absolute value, and write R=K∘R=K^\circR=K∘. Let X\mathcal XX be an integral projective flat RRR-scheme with smooth integral projective generic fibre XXX of dimension nnn. Write D=d′d′′D=d'd''D=d′d′′, and use Mihatsch’s actual sheaf B\mathcal BB on the ordinary analytic topology. In its intrinsic trigrading, B0,0,r\mathcal B^{0,0,r}B0,0,r has bidegree (r,r)(r,r)(r,r). All current comparisons in this section may be restricted to the original smooth CLD test forms.

The analytic inputs used below are the following primary-source results. Mihatsch, δ\deltaδ-Forms on Lubin–Tate spaces, arXiv:2112.10018v4, Definition 4.2, Remark 4.3(1), Lemma 4.4, Theorem 4.5, Definition 4.10 and Proposition 4.11 provide the actual sheaf, pullback, coefficientwise multiplication by PWS forms, integration, Stokes, and the injective map to currents commuting with d′,d′′d',d''d′,d′′. The paragraph following his Theorem 5.3 identifies model first Chern forms with elements of B0,0,1\mathcal B^{0,0,1}B0,0,1. Gubler–Martin, On Zhang’s semipositive metrics, Theorem 1.1 and Proposition 2.15 give algebraization of model metrics on a proper variety and uniform density of rational model functions. Chambert-Loir–Ducros, arXiv:1204.6277v2, Corollary 17.8.9, §8.8.5 and Theorem 18.5.5 give the difference-of-psh decomposition, the multilinear Bedford–Taylor product, and its native model mass formula. Proposition 18.5.8 gives the component multiplicities on a relatively normal model over the discretely valued field KKK. These references are numbered as in the PDF, rather than the flattened section counters of its HTML rendering.

Lemma 2.1 (Comparison of actual model products and Bedford–Taylor products). For any finite list of model metrized algebraic line bundles on XXX, the current of the actual wedge of their first Chern forms equals their CLD multilinear curvature product, when tested against original smooth forms. In top degree the two sides therefore define the same signed Radon measure. This assertion holds over KKK itself.

Proof. Work on an ordinary open on which the bundles are trivial, and write ui=−log⁡∥si∥u_i=-\log\|s_i\|ui​=−log∥si​∥ for their continuous PWS weights. By Corollary 17.8.9 of CLD, model metrized line bundles on a projective analytification are differences of psh metrized line bundles. The identity can consequently be proved by induction for psh factors and extended by multilinearity. The local weights and all products below are actual forms; in particular DuiDu_iDui​ is the actual first curvature.

The induction step requires a multiplication statement, which we make explicit. Let TTT be the actual product of the already treated curvatures. Its current has order zero: on a common moment presentation, pairing TTT with a fixed compactly supported smooth complementary form gives a finite sum of signed measures with smooth coefficient densities on polyhedra. For a continuous PWS weight uuu, Mihatsch’s coefficientwise formula in Remark 4.3(1) gives [uT](η)=∫u dμT,η,μT,η the measure of T∧η.[uT](\eta)=\int u\,d\mu_{T,\eta}, \qquad \mu_{T,\eta}\text{ the measure of }T\wedge\eta .[uT](η)=∫udμT,η​,μT,η​ the measure of T∧η. The formula can be checked on a finite ordinary cover of the support of η\etaη and then summed using smooth partitions. Thus it is independent of the common moment presentation. By the induction hypothesis, [T][T][T] is the CLD curvature product. Its standard continuous multiplication by uuu gives precisely the same coefficient measures. Equivalently, equality on smooth scalar multipliers extends to continuous scalar multipliers by uniform approximation on each compact support. Hence [uT]=u[T][uT]=u[T][uT]=u[T].

The factors of TTT are separately closed. Actual Leibniz and the chain-map assertion of Mihatsch’s Proposition 4.11 now give [Du∧T]=[D(uT)]=D[uT]=D(u[T]).[Du\wedge T]=[D(uT)]=D[uT]=D\bigl(u[T]\bigr).[Du∧T]=[D(uT)]=D[uT]=D(u[T]). This is the defining Bedford–Taylor recursion, with its extension to differences of psh functions supplied by CLD §8.8.5. The induction starts with the fundamental integration current and proves the assertion in every degree. In top degree, these currents are Radon measures and equality on smooth scalar tests determines the measure. No scalar extension or general product of arbitrary currents occurs. ◻

Theorem 2.4 (Strict actual Chern forms of model vector bundles). For model vector bundles E1,…,Es\mathcal E_1,\ldots,\mathcal E_sE1​,…,Es​ on X\mathcal XX and a homogeneous rational Chern polynomial PPP of degree rrr, 1≤r≤n1\le r\le n1≤r≤n, there is a unique separately closed actual form cX(P)∈B0,0,r(Xan)c_{\mathcal X}(P)\in\mathcal B^{0,0,r}(X^{\mathrm{an}})cX​(P)∈B0,0,r(Xan) whose pullback to the simultaneous full flag bundle is the corresponding model-root polynomial. The construction is functorial under morphisms of integral projective flat models with smooth integral generic fibres. Polynomial operational identities, including Whitney identities, Chern-character additivity and Adams identities, hold as strict identities of actual forms. Numerical triviality of the special-fibre polynomial implies cX(P)=0c_{\mathcal X}(P)=0cX​(P)=0.

Proof. Let a:F=∏XFlag⁡(Ej)→Xa:\mathcal F=\prod_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Flag}(\mathcal E_j) \to\mathcal Xa:F=∏X​Flag(Ej​)→X and write ΩF\Omega_FΩF​ for its model-root polynomial. Flag bundles, and their fibre products here, are integral projective flat models; their generic fibres are smooth integral varieties. On F×XF\mathcal F\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal FF×X​F, the two root polynomials represent the same operational Chern class, by the two tautological filtrations. Thus their difference restricts to the zero operational class on the special fibre. It is a polynomial in first Chern classes of model line bundles, so Theorem 2.3, applied in the dimension of this larger generic fibre, proves p1∗ΩF=p2∗ΩF(H22.C2)p_1^*\Omega_F=p_2^*\Omega_F \tag{H22.C2}p1∗​ΩF​=p2∗​ΩF​(H22.C2) as actual forms.

Trivialize the finitely many generic bundles simultaneously on Zariski opens Ui⊂XU_i\subset XUi​⊂X. Their standard flags give algebraic sections si:Ui→Fs_i:U_i\to Fsi​:Ui​→F. These are genuine analytic sections on ordinary opens after analytification. All their domains and targets are pure-dimensional and boundaryless, so Mihatsch’s Theorem 4.5 applies even though the sections need not extend to the models. Pulling ({H22.C2}) back by (si,sj)(s_i,s_j)(si​,sj​) proves that si∗ΩFs_i^*\Omega_Fsi∗​ΩF​ glue to an actual form cX(P)c_{\mathcal X}(P)cX​(P). The sections also make a∗a^*a∗ injective, proving uniqueness. Pullback respects tridegree and differentials, so the descended form is pure and separately closed.

To prove a universal operational identity among finitely many bundles, take their simultaneous flag bundle and subtract the corresponding root polynomials. The difference is zero in special-fibre operational Chow. The preceding theorem makes it zero as an actual form upstairs; injectivity of flag pullback gives the strict identity downstairs. This proves Whitney and additive relations. For a morphism of the specified models, pull back the flag bundle and its tautological line quotients. Model first Chern forms are functorial, so the pulled-back form and the newly constructed form have the same characteristic flag pullback. Faithfulness of that pullback proves functoriality. The same argument with the product of two splitting presentations proves independence of presentation. In particular a model refinement leaves the actual form of a fixed pulled-back model bundle unchanged.

Theorem 2.3 kills ΩF\Omega_FΩF​ and the local sections kill its descent. This proves the last assertion. ◻

Scope of the conclusion.

The preceding construction uses no finite trace and no prescribed Green-pair theorem. It supplies the strict model-Chern input used in Sections 3 and 8. It does not identify two arbitrary model extensions merely because their generic bundles are isomorphic; that comparison requires the separate global-primitive argument. It also makes no assertion that the curvature of every geometrically homologically trivial cycle is exact.

3. The minimal trace needed by a supported perfect complex

The scalar–curvature module.

The supported-complex Green formula needs only expressions u0 Du1⋯Duk,D=d′d′′,(MT1)u_0\,Du_1\cdots Du_k, \qquad D=d'd'', \tag{MT1}u0​Du1​⋯Duk​,D=d′d′′,(MT1) with PL scalar potentials. A single parameter evaluates the whole scalar coefficient u0u_0u0​, even when u0u_0u0​ is nonlinear PL in many moment coordinates. The proof constructs this trace directly from scalar PL descent, max/min sorting, and Euclidean projection. The inputs are specified below; a trace on arbitrary actual forms or a universal Green-pair construction is not assumed.

Throughout this section KKK is a complete nontrivially valued field of characteristic zero, and all analytic spaces are the analytifications of normal integral separated KKK-varieties, with their ordinary topology. All forms are Mihatsch actual delta-forms. A PL scalar means a function locally presented by a finite piecewise affine function of logarithms of analytic units. Its DDD is a pure form of tridegree (0,0,1)(0,0,1)(0,0,1). Let Mk\mathscr M^kMk be the actual image sheaf of finite sums of ({MT1}). Relations in Mk\mathscr M^kMk are actual-form relations; no chosen presentation is part of a section.

3.1. Primary analytic inputs and native degree

We use the following statements in their stated scopes.

  1. Mihatsch, Delta-Forms on Lubin–Tate Spaces, arXiv:2112.10018v4, Definition 4.2 and Theorem 4.5: local Euclidean presentations, the ordinary sheaf, arbitrary actual pullback between pure-dimensional boundaryless spaces, and compatibility with products and differential operators.

  2. Ibid., Remark 4.3(1), Lemma 4.4, Corollary 4.9 and Proposition 4.11: coefficientwise multiplication by a PWS scalar on a witnessing skeleton; support avoidance when the maximum bidegree exceeds the algebraic dimension; Stokes; and injectivity into ordinary CLD currents.

  3. Ibid., Definition 3.4 and Lemmas 3.3 and 3.15: native calibrated tropical weights and the finite-flat degree formula. These are used for top forms only.

  4. Ibid., Proposition 2.17, Definition 2.29(3), Lemma 2.37, Proposition 2.38 and Definition 2.41: proper-on-support pushforward of polyhedral currents on weighted pwl spaces, its differential compatibility, and the boundary-excluded chart characterization of tropical pullback. Definition 3.8, Remark 3.9 and the coordinate case of the proof of Proposition 3.21 identify product skeletons with their linear functions and native weights. Definition 4.10 defines analytic integration intrinsically on skeletons.

  5. Mihatsch, On Tropical Intersection Theory, arXiv:2107.12067v3, Section 2.3, Example 2.5, Theorem 4.1(3), and Proposition/Definition 4.2: affine proper-on-support Euclidean pushforward, its projection formula, and affine pullback.

This argument does not construct a trace of arbitrary source coefficients. It also proves that finite dominant pullback on actual forms is faithful: pair a putatively zero pullback with pulled-back original-smooth complementary tests, use ({MT2}), and apply Proposition 4.11.

3.2. Only scalar PL functions pass through a finite quotient

Lemma 3.1 (Ordinary local scalar PL descent). Let q:Y→Xq:Y\to Xq:Y→X be finite Galois between normal integral varieties, with group GGG. 3.4. Certified integration along a parameter torus

The boundary issue.

Compact analytic support does not imply that an ambient moment coefficient avoids the tropicalized analytic boundary of an affinoid chart. We do not use the single-chart integral formula with that unverified hypothesis. Instead we first prove a pushforward identity for polyhedral currents on the product skeleton, retaining the boundary exclusion of Proposition 2.38 at every chart calculation. The intrinsic skeletal definition of integration then gives the analytic pairing. In this subsection f⋆f^\starf⋆ denotes tropical-space pullback in that proposition, distinguished from the notation tc∗t_c^*tc∗​ for the resulting actual analytic form.

The inverse is (p,v(z))(p,v(z))(p,v(z)) on the displayed skeleton. It is pwl: a base skeleton chart is described by an affinoid domain and valuations of its analytic units; their pullbacks are valuations of the same units on the product, and v(z)v(z)v(z) is the extra coordinate. 3.5. The minimal finite trace theorem

Its parameter-uniform assertion supplies a product-moment presentation, so multiplication by χ(t)t\chi(t)tχ(t)t and application of IpXI_{p_X}IpX​​ are legitimate.

Pair with an arbitrary compact actual test η\etaη. First Lemma 3.6, then ({MT5}) with the actual downstairs multiplier χ(t)t pX∗η\chi(t)t\,p_X^*\etaχ(t)tpX∗​η, and finally Lemma 3.7, give ∫XTr⁡qM(ω)η=∫X×Gmχ(t)t Tr⁡q×id⁡curv(DH∏iDui) pX∗η=∫Y×Gmχ(t)t DH∏iDui pY∗q∗η=∫Yu0∏iDui q∗η.\begin{split} \int_X\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathscr M}_q(\omega)\eta &=\int_{X\times\mathbf G_m}\chi(t)t\, \operatorname{Tr}^{\rm curv}_{q\times\operatorname{id}} (DH\prod_iDu_i)\,p_X^*\eta\\ &=\int_{Y\times\mathbf G_m}\chi(t)t\,DH\prod_iDu_i\, p_Y^*q^*\eta\\ &=\int_Yu_0\prod_iDu_i\,q^*\eta. \end{split}∫X​TrqM​(ω)η​=∫X×Gm​​χ(t)tTrq×idcurv​(DHi∏​Dui​)pX∗​η=∫Y×Gm​​χ(t)tDHi∏​Dui​pY∗​q∗η=∫Y​u0​i∏​Dui​q∗η.​ All these integrals have compact paired support. The identity is proved for all actual tests, not merely for model or original-smooth tests. Add generators. If an expression represents zero as an actual source form, its trace has zero pairing with every test, and is zero by Proposition 4.11. The same argument removes dependence on the cutoff, source moments, quotient moments, Galois closure, and all local choices. It also glues the local answers in the ordinary topology and proves uniqueness. ◻

Limits of this theorem.

It is enough for a PL scalar times a model Chern polynomial, since model line curvatures locally have PL potentials. It does not assert a trace for an arbitrary source delta-form, and it does not assert an analytic proper pushforward for a positive-dimensional proper map. Normality of the target is retained throughout. The Galois quotient and native calibration arguments do not replace the original field by an algebraic closure. The theorem is independently derived above; its use should be labelled as this internal minimal trace, rather than as an externally published finite-trace result.

Proposition 4.3 (Ordinary scalar descent with fixed parameter moments). Let KKK be complete, nontrivially valued and of characteristic zero. Let q:Y→Xq:Y\to Xq:Y→X be a finite dominant morphism of normal integral separated algebraic KKK-varieties whose function-field extension is Galois with group GGG. A GGG-invariant PL scalar on YanY^{\mathrm{an}}Yan descends locally in the ordinary topology to a PL scalar on XanX^{\mathrm{an}}Xan.

For the parameter version, fix x∈Xanx\in X^{\mathrm{an}}x∈Xan and an ordinary neighborhood UUU of xxx. Suppose finitely many invariant scalar functions on q−1U×Gmanq^{-1}U\times\mathbf G_m^{\mathrm{an}}q−1U×Gman​ admit presentations Fi(y,z)=φi(ℓ(y),t(z)),ℓ=(v(f1),…,v(fs)),t=v(z),F_i(y,z)=\varphi_i(\ell(y),t(z)),\qquad \ell=(v(f_1),\ldots,v(f_s)),\quad t=v(z),Fi​(y,z)=φi​(ℓ(y),t(z)),ℓ=(v(f1​),…,v(fs​)),t=v(z), where fjf_jfj​ are a fixed tuple of analytic units on q−1Uq^{-1}Uq−1U and φi\varphi_iφi​ are finite PL functions on the whole Euclidean moment space. After shrinking UUU around xxx, there are a fixed tuple of base analytic units bbb and finite PL functions Ψi\Psi_iΨi​ such that Fi=q∗Ψi(v(b),t).F_i=q^*\Psi_i(v(b),t).Fi​=q∗Ψi​(v(b),t). The base tuple and shrinking are independent of every t∈Rt\in\mathbf Rt∈R.

Proof. For the nonparameter assertion, choose disjoint relatively compact ordinary neighborhoods of the finitely many points of q−1(x)q^{-1}(x)q−1(x), small enough for moment presentations of the prescribed scalars. Properness of qanq^{\mathrm{an}}qan gives an ordinary neighborhood UUU of xxx whose full inverse image lies in their union. The source pieces are clopen in q−1Uq^{-1}Uq−1U. Paste analytic units across these pieces, inserting constant units on the other pieces. Use one additional pasted constant unit with different valuations to distinguish the pieces. Nontriviality of the valuation supplies arbitrarily many such constants. By the initial shrinking the source moment images lie in finitely many disjoint compact boxes. A finite triangulation of a surrounding compact box, subordinate to these boxes and to the scalar affine cells, extends each of their finite PL functions. Extending beyond the surrounding box by coordinatewise clipping gives one finite PL presentation on the full source moment space.

In the parameter case the stipulated common presentation is the starting point; no extension from arbitrary unbounded disjoint cylinders is needed. Enlarge the source tuple by its GGG-orbit. The group now acts by coordinate permutations. Average each ambient presentation over GGG. Invariance on the source shows that averaging does not change the represented scalar function, while it produces an invariant finite PL function on the whole Euclidean space. Apply Lemma 4.2, with or without the parameter.

6. The product skeleton and its topology

Proposition 6.1 (Coordinate Gauss product). Let VVV be a boundaryless ordinary analytic open of pure dimension nnn in an algebraic KKK-analytic space, and let bbb be a finite tuple of analytic units on VVV. Put S=Σ(V,b)S=\Sigma(V,b)S=Σ(V,b). The relative Gauss section identifies S×R ≃ Σ(V×Gman,(b,z)),(y,t)⟼νt(y),(TD2)S\times\mathbf R\ \simeq\ \Sigma(V\times\mathbf G_m^{\mathrm{an}},(b,z)),\qquad (y,t)\longmapsto\nu_t(y), \tag{TD2}S×R ≃ Σ(V×Gman​,(b,z)),(y,t)⟼νt​(y),(TD2) as weighted pwl spaces with their specified linear function sheaves. The weight is the base weight times the standard weight on R\mathbf RR. The identification respects ordinary restriction and every additional base moment tuple.

Proof. The skeleton criterion is the graded-transcendence-degree criterion of [1, §3.1]. A point above yyy has degree n+1n+1n+1 in the moments (b,z)(b,z)(b,z) if and only if bbb has degree nnn at yyy and the graded reduction of zzz is transcendental over H(y)~\widetilde{\mathcal H(y)}H(y)​. For this equivalence, once the base degree is nnn, the full graded residue field of yyy is algebraic over the field generated by bbb. The last condition means precisely that every Laurent polynomial has the Gauss norm ∣∑iaizi∣=max⁡i∣ai(y)∣e−it.\left|\sum_i a_i z^i\right|=\max_i |a_i(y)|e^{-it}.​i∑​ai​zi​=imax​∣ai​(y)∣e−it. It thus specifies the unique point νt(y)\nu_t(y)νt​(y). This proves the bijection in ({TD2}), without extending KKK or restricting the radius.

Here are the topology details. On an affinoid base domain and a compact annulus in the parameter, analytic functions have uniformly convergent Laurent expansions. Their values on the Gauss section are limits of the finite maxima displayed above, uniformly on that domain times the parameter interval. They are continuous in (y,t)(y,t)(y,t). The Gauss section is therefore continuous locally, hence globally. Its inverse is the continuous map (p,v(z))(p,v(z))(p,v(z)) on its image. Equivalently, its image over a compact base set and a compact interval is closed inside the corresponding compact relative annulus, since the displayed Gauss equalities are closed conditions and determine the image uniquely. This verifies, when needed, the properness claim used in the product-integration argument.

The inverse map is pwl for the skeleton atlases: a pwl chart on a base skeleton is locally described by valuations of analytic units on an affinoid domain; their pullbacks, together with v(z)v(z)v(z), give the same coordinate functions upstairs. Analytic-domain restrictions and their inverse images restrict the corresponding pwl charts. After taking finite polyhedral charts, this continuous bijective pwl map is a pwl isomorphism. Indeed subdivide until each piece is affine. Injectivity makes each linear part injective on the span of its piece, so its inverse is affine on the image. Properness on compact charts and a common image subdivision make these inverse pieces a locally finite pwl atlas. This is also the coordinate case of the atlas argument following (3.31) in [1].

On a top-dimensional base cell, compute its native weight by a generic toric projection that is locally finite flat, as in the definition of the skeleton weight. Its product with the identity on the parameter torus is finite flat of the same degree. Hence the weight on the product cell is the base weight times the standard parameter weight. All residue and field-degree factors are retained. The moment tuple is literally (b,z)(b,z)(b,z), so the specified sheaf of linear functions is generated by the base linear functions and ttt. Adding base moments uses the same relative Gauss section and the same degrees; restriction does likewise. This proves all the claimed compatibilities. ◻

Why ordinary flag sections alone do not replace this step.

The model-Chern construction in Section 2 descends forms by local sections because the upstairs Chern form satisfies its fiber-product cocycle identity. A primitive on a flag bundle need not satisfy that identity: pulling it to two sections only produces forms whose difference is DDD-closed. The present argument does not infer Green descent from Chern descent. Its use of a finite multisection is exactly where the minimal trace is subsequently applied.

Proof. Write each algebraic line bundle as a quotient of two very ample ones. Choose PWS metrics on those factors so that their quotient is the given metric. Expand PPP by multilinearity. For each resulting monomial, choose a section of each very ample factor successively, meeting the finitely many current integral cycle components properly. The infinite field KKK supplies such choices. Work componentwise when an intermediate divisor is reducible or nonreduced.

At every step apply scalar strong Poincare–Lelong, Mihatsch Corollary 5.6, with the remaining closed curvature factors and the pullback of η\etaη as test. The latter is separately closed because η\etaη is top-degree on AAA. The Green correction is therefore zero. One is left with the pullback of η\etaη integrated on a cycle of dimension mmm.

A component mapping to a lower-dimensional subset of AAA contributes zero, because the support of the actual top test avoids that subset. For a dominating component, remove a proper closed subset of AAA so that the component maps finite flat of its native generic degree. The top test again avoids the removed subset. The native finite degree formula evaluates the integral with exactly that degree. This is precisely algebraic proper pushforward of the terminal intersection cycle, proving ({PC6}). ◻

This lemma is an all-actual-test scalar equality. It does not define the proper pushforward of an arbitrary actual form. It applies to each Dα→ZjD_\alpha\to Z_jDα​→Zj​ in ({PC5}), with m=n−rm=n-rm=n−r and t=r−1t=r-1t=r−1. Components whose image has smaller dimension contribute zero by the same support argument.

These finitely many generic bundle complexes extend to a common projective model after a vertical modification. For completeness, extend each bundle coherently, twist to obtain finitely many generators, and close the graph of its generic quotient in a Grassmann bundle. Its tautological quotient is a model vector bundle with the original generic fiber. Use the product of the finitely many Grassmann bundles. Every generic differential extends after multiplying by a common power of a uniformizer; the resulting successive products are zero because they vanish on the dense generic fiber. The scaled generic complex is chain-isomorphic to the original one by degreewise scalar rescaling. Its full model cohomology support has generic support exactly ZjZ_jZj​.

9. The supported-complex construction over a nongeometrically integral base

Lemma 9.1 (Native integral scope of the supported-complex construction). Keep the original finite extension K/QpK/\mathbf Q_pK/Qp​ and its absolute value. The supported-complex theorem of Section 8, the exact-support Green-pair construction for every prescribed rational cycle, and the generic-Chow-zero global primitive construction apply to every smooth integral projective KKK-variety XXX. Geometric integrality over KKK is not required. Every actual form, test and finite-trace operation in these statements is in the original KKK-analytic theory.

Proof. The supported-complex section and its main theorem already assume only that XXX is smooth and integral. We check the one potentially sensitive ingredient and then the passage to an arbitrary prescribed cycle, whose preceding corollary was stated with the stronger hypothesis.

Let F→YF\to YF→Y be the smooth projective flag fibration appearing after the kernel-Grassmann modification and its characteristic-zero generic resolution. Both FFF and YYY are smooth integral KKK-varieties. Put d=dim⁡F−dim⁡Yd=\dim F-\dim Yd=dimF−dimY. If d=0d=0d=0, the map is already finite etale and its integral source can be used. If d>0d>0d>0, the uniform fiber dimension argument in Lemma 8.1 gives a nonempty open of tuples of high-degree very ample sections whose common zero locus has finite nonempty fibers over every point of YYY. Its dimension estimate is made on every geometric fiber and does not require the total space or the base to be geometrically integral.

Intersect this parameter open with the smooth complete-intersection Bertini open. The latter requires smoothness of the source and a linear system giving an immersion, not geometric irreducibility; these are exactly the hypotheses of Stacks Lemma 33.47.3, Tag 0FD6. Successive restrictions of the very ample linear system still give immersions. Equivalently, after algebraic base change the smoothness conditions are imposed simultaneously on the finitely many geometric components; the resulting nonempty open is defined over KKK. Since KKK is infinite it has a KKK-rational tuple. No analytic scalar extension is involved in this algebraic check.

The resulting complete intersection T0allT_0^{\rm all}T0all​ is smooth, projective, and of pure dimension dim⁡Y\dim YdimY. Its map to YYY is proper with finite nonempty fibers, hence finite surjective. Miracle flatness applies, since its source is Cohen–Macaulay and YYY is regular; see Stacks Tag 00R4. Every connected component of a regular scheme is integral, because its irreducible components are disjoint. Choose any nonempty connected component T0T_0T0​. It is open and closed in T0allT_0^{\rm all}T0all​, so its finite map is still flat. Its image is both open and closed in integral YYY, and therefore all of YYY. Consequently T0→YT_0\to YT0​→Y is smooth-source, integral, finite flat and surjective, with its own native positive degree.

Choosing this component does not spoil the supported K0K_0K0​ identity: the identity is pulled back to the chosen component, rather than being an equality that would require summing the classes of all components of a fixed intersection cycle. Subsequent target-flag graph closures and generic resolutions are birational on this integral source and preserve its full prescribed finite open. The leading supported-character identity then uses f∗[T]=d[X]f_*[T]=d[X]f∗​[T]=d[X] with this actual function-field degree ddd. Normality needed by the minimal trace follows from smoothness of the generic source and target. None of these statements requires geometric integrality.

For a prescribed cycle Z=∑jaj[Zj]Z=\sum_j a_j[Z_j]Z=∑j​aj​[Zj​] on this XXX, resolve each OZj\mathcal O_{Z_j}OZj​​ by finitely many generic vector bundles. Such resolutions use regularity and the projective resolution property, which hold for smooth integral XXX over KKK. Extend the bundles by the same finite Grassmann-graph construction to a projective flat model, and extend the differentials after uniformizer rescaling. Each model complex has generic support exactly ZjZ_jZj​. The preceding supported-complex theorem applies component by component. Summing with the nonzero coefficients gives a Green pair on exactly Xan∖∣Z∣anX^{\rm an}\setminus|Z|^{\rm an}Xan∖∣Z∣an, with the original cycle and all actual tests retained. This proves the stated extension of the exact-support corollary.

The global primitive proof uses the same construction with generic open U=XU=XU=X. Generic K0K_0K0​ relations, Grassmann subbundle graphs, and rational Adams projectors require smooth integral projectivity, not geometric integrality. Their primitives consequently retain the original global scalar-curvature line sums and finite-flat maps over KKK, as in Section 8. ◻

Remark 30 (Finite constant extensions are treated as native schemes). Let K′/KK'/KK′/K be finite and let Y/K′Y/K'Y/K′ be smooth integral projective. The composite Y→Spec⁡KY\to\operatorname{Spec}KY→SpecK is smooth because K′/KK'/KK′/K is separable, and it is still integral and projective. A projective flat R′R'R′-model of YYY is projective and flat over RRR. Lemma 9.1 can therefore be run directly on this RRR-model, producing KKK-actual forms and testing against arbitrary KKK-actual tests. This is not an inference from a formula tested only over K′K'K′.

The special fiber over RRR keeps its ramification thickening, and the degree of a finite generic map is its full degree as a KKK-morphism. Thus no comparison of native skeleton measures over different ground fields is required for this scope clarification. The present lemma makes this native treatment explicit for the exact-support corollary.
